title: Counting the Last Day of the Interest Span on a Telephone Payment for an Auto Loan
content:
Whether the last day of the interest span counts, when a payment is taken on the telephone on a loan of the Auto Loans line, turns on two readings of the borrower's Personal Checking account.

**Basis questions**

**Which two readings?** Whether the borrower holds an active checking account whose posted balance is at least the fee-waiver daily balance its tier publishes, and whether at least 2 recurring deposits have posted to that account in the last three months.

**What follows where both hold?** The last day of the span is dropped.

**What follows where exactly one of the two holds?** The span is counted as it stands.

**What follows where neither holds?** A further day is added to the span.

**Does it matter which of the two holds?** No. Where exactly one holds, the outcome is the same whichever it is.

**How is the deposit reading counted?** As the number of recurring deposits posted to that same active checking account over the three months ending today. A borrower with 2 such deposits meets the reading; a borrower with 1 does not.

**What is the balance compared against?** The fee-waiver daily balance published for the tier of Personal Checking that the borrower's active account belongs to, so the comparison figure moves with that account's tier.

## The three outcomes on a span of 30 days

Where both readings hold, the span counts 29 days. Where exactly one holds, it counts 30. Where neither holds, it counts 31.
